- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or fails to capture sharp drops; increase forecast sensitivity to negative sentiment.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (especially in last 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor to forecasts after high sentiment spikes.
- Mean reversion is strong in early 2025 data — model often overestimates mid-term trends; adjust forecasts downward if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms in late-period (last 5–7 days) — especially when sentiment is low; add lagged sentiment correction to recent days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model tends to miss the rebound; anticipate and slightly boost forecast in 3–5 days after negative sentiment ends.
